items.q: What kind of "temperament" does SML most resemble below?
options: Declarative notes that can save quotation marks/commas
items.explain: SML is a declarative data/configuration format where quotation marks and commas can be omitted, and the structure is delimited by {}, like writing notes.

items.q: Which of the following statements is correct?
options: SML must be written as a strict JSON tree
The SML parsing result is a language independent key value tree
items.explain: The parsing result (key value tree) of SML is isomorphic in Rust/C/JS/Lua, which is precisely why it is cross language friendly.

items.q: In SML, which symbol below can be annotated?
items.explain: SML supports three types of line comments (up to the end of the line): #, --, and//, as well as/*... */block comments (across lines); There are also _ *... * _ as alternative block annotation styles.

ch01.title: Chapter 1 Self testing: Basic Key Values

items.q: Which line in SML will parse NY into a string (instead of an error)?
items.explain: The bare word of SML defaults to a string, and state: NY is equivalent to state: "NY".

items.q: Judgment: After parsing age: 27, 27 is an integer instead of a string.
items.explain: Numbers without quotation marks will be parsed as numeric types (integers/floating points), and the age field is an integer of 27.

items.q: Which of the following values is a scalar type supported by SML?
items.explain: SML scalars support boolean, null, integer, floating-point, and string; The essence of a date is a string and there is no specific date type.

items.q: Do I need to write "hello" as a value in Chinese?
options: No need, just use bare words
items.explain: Chinese and other non ASCII naked words themselves are strings, city: Beijing is legal and does not require quotation marks.

ch02.title: Chapter 2 Self Test: Blocks and Arrays

items.q: Is the result of writing address { city: NY } and address: { city: NY } the same?
options: Different, the first one is an array
items.explain: The colon before the block in SML can be omitted, and address { } is equivalent to address: { }, both of which are object blocks.

items.q: Which of the following can correctly represent an array?
items.explain: The array is wrapped in square brackets [ ]; The elements within square brackets are separated by spaces, and commas can also be omitted.

items.q: What is the correct intra row object { name: alice role: admin }?
options: Fields must be separated by commas
items.explain: Fields within the line objects { } are separated by spaces, with role: admin following closely behind name: alice.

items.q: Judgment: SML arrays can mix different types, such as [ 1 "two" true ].
items.explain: SML does not restrict array element types, [ 1 "two" true ] is a valid heterogeneous array.

items.q: Which symbol is used to define reusable fragments?
items.explain: @base { } defines fragment templates, and&base references them elsewhere for inheritance and merging.

items.q: In service auth { &base port: 7100 }, if @base has already defined port: 7000, what is the result port?
items.explain: After referencing&base, the local field will overwrite the same named field in the fragment, with a port of 7100.

items.q: Judgment:&base must be placed on the first line of the block to take effect.
options: Yes, it must be the first field
items.explain: &The base reference can appear at any field position within the block, and SML will first perform fragment merging before parsing other fields.

items.q: What problems does fragment inheritance mainly solve?
items.explain: Fragments are used to extract and reuse common fields such as region/timeout to avoid duplicate writing for each service.

ch04.title: Chapter 4 Self testing: Include and namespace

items.q: What is the purpose of including "ui" as ui?
options: Merge the content of ui.sml into the root
Load ui.sml into the UI namespace
items.explain: Hang the parsing results of the included files in the UI namespace and access them using ui.title to avoid naming conflicts.

items.q: Where does the UI come from when writing title: ui.title as the main file?
options: Variables defined in the current file
items.explain: ui.title refers to the title field in the namespace loaded with include "ui" as ui.

items.q: Judgment: 'include' can introduce multiple files, each of which can use 'as' to start a different namespace.
items.explain: You can include "a" as a and "b" as b multiple times, each isolated and not polluting the root namespace.

items.q: Will the glob include "modules/*. sml" as m?
options: Load all matching files into the m namespace
items.explain: After enabling the globe feature, all files matched by *. sml will be batch loaded into the m namespace.

items.q: What does loose mean in @contract Server loose { port: int min 1024 }?
options: Allow extra fields outside the contract
items.explain: The SML contract defaults to strict (rejecting undeclared fields) and allows for additional fields only when written as loose; Min 1024 is the lower bound constraint for the port.

items.q: port: int min 1024 max 65535， Which of the following values will fail verification?
items.explain: If 80 is less than min 1024, contract verification will report an error; The rest are within the [1024, 65535] range.

items.q: What does role: enum(user, admin, owner) mean by default user?
options: Role can only take one of the three options
Default user when role is omitted
items.explain: Enum limits the set of values, default fills in the default value 'user' when the field is not provided.

items.q: Judgment: Data written after @is Server with incorrect field types will also be blocked by the contract.
items.explain: The contract will check the field type, for example, if a field declaring str is written as a number, the verification will fail.

ch06.title: Chapter 6 Self testing: Environment Variables and Escaping

items.q: What syntax is used to inject environment variables into values?
items.explain: SML injects the values of environment variables into $env.NAME during the parsing period.

items.q: What does $env.X usually parse into when running Playground in a browser?
items.explain: The front-end JS parser cannot access real environment variables, and when $env.X cannot be retrieved, it will be parsed as an empty string, which is the expected behavior.

items.q: Judgment: \u{1F680} will be escaped as an emoji character in the string.
items.explain: SML supports \u{...} code point escape, \u{1F680} is 🚀。

items.q: Which escape is supported by SML?
items.explain: SML supports common escape schemes such as \n, \t, \", etc; C-style byte escaping such as \x41 is not its standard escape form.

items.q: What is the behavior of SML contracts in multiple languages?
options: Each language implements it on its own and may not be consistent
items.explain: The parsing results and contract validation of SML are isomorphic and consistent in Rust/C/JS/Lua, which is the core selling point.

items.q: Judgment: The field names and nested structures obtained from parsing the same SML file using Rust and Lua should be exactly the same.
items.explain: This is precisely the manifestation of SML's cross language friendliness: data isomorphism, host language is just a carrier.

items.q: Which export is usually used to call a parser in JS?
items.explain: sml.mjs exports parse/parseSafe (with error object return), which is the actual entrance used by the front-end playground.

items.q: What capabilities are typically combined in a real deployment configuration?
items.explain: Practical projects often involve contracts include、 Use fragments, $env, and features together to form a maintainable configuration.

items.q: What type is peers: [ auth billing ]?
items.explain: The naked word auth billing in square brackets is parsed as a string array ["auth","billing"].

items.q: Judgment: It is a good practice for database: { url: $env.DATABASE_URL } to leave sensitive information outside the source code.
items.explain: Inject password/connection string with $env to avoid writing the key in the configuration file.

items.q: What does contract combination refer to?
options: Reuse small contracts as field types
items.explain: If the Endpoint contract is reused by Service's main: Endpoint and array[Endpoint], it forms a type combination.

items.q: Which mode is suitable for "multi environment shared basic configuration"?
items.explain: Extract the common fields into @base fragments, and include them in each environment to overwrite the different fields, making it the easiest to maintain.

items.q: Judgment: array[Endpoint]? At the end? Indicates that this field can be omitted.
items.explain: This field is optional (null/default) and will not trigger a contract error if not provided.

items.q: Is it recommended to use "pre validation" in design patterns?
items.explain: Using strict contract+@ is to verify can expose incorrect configurations as early as possible at the configuration loading entry

items.q: Which feature should be used to enable the include feature in Glob configuration?
items.explain: The syntax is @feature enable glob, and only when enabled can include "x/*. sml" be compatible.

items.q: Judgment: Without declaring @feature, all SML basic syntax (key value/block/array/contract) is still available.
items.explain: Features only control optional/extended syntax, core syntax is enabled by default and does not require declaration.

items.q: Which of the following belongs to the expansion capability of feature control?
items.explain: Glob and implicit ns are feature switching terms; Naked words and $env are basic syntax.

items.q: What are the common mistakes in writing @feature (such as spelling a wrong name)?
items.explain: The parser will recognize unknown feature names and report an error, indicating a list of available features.

items.q: What is the significant difference between SML and JSON?
options: The structure relies on {} instead of indentation
Root object name must be written
items.explain: SML naked word quotation marks, spaces/line breaks separated by commas, delimited by curly braces; There is no need to strictly add quotation marks and commas like JSON.

items.q: Judgment: SML's contract system (@contract) does not have a direct equivalent in JSON Schema.
items.explain: SML builds the contract into the configuration language itself, while JSON requires an additional schema file, and the two are positioned differently.

items.q: When troubleshooting 'fields not yet effective', prioritize checking?
items.explain: The ineffective configuration is often due to misspelling of field names, lack of namespace references, or discarding redundant fields in strict contracts.
